hypotheses.confidence_note: Conditional local two-second prototype, not verified world safety. PREMISE_SPACE repair: the finite prototype_local_scope delimits the road task and entrant exclusions only; it is no longer bound as support for actor scenarios or sources extending outside that patch. Those complete, unchanged BODY sources are supported by their explicit actor-motion premises with space_polygon_m=null. No road enlargement, obstacle removal, source contraction or residual reduction was used. All five previously declared actors are retained. The ego is moving at 1.679 m/s; approximately 1.2 m/s^2 braking stops in 1.4 s and 1.18 m, within the supplied limits, subject to verification. Metric geometry and residuals are uncalibrated model hypotheses. The prototype excludes distant traffic rows, the rear intersection and sidewalk activity under the explicit no-entry conditions in prototype_local_scope. Observed pedestrians at the side-street corners and beside the right parked sedan are conditionally assumed to remain outside the local road patch; this is falsifiable, not evidence that they are absent. Actor predictions outside the road patch remain represented and checked. No optimizer, independent verifier or simulated prefix has been run here.

premises.statement: The local driving task is restricted to this finite continuous paved roadway patch over [0,2] seconds, including the current ego footprint and proposed stopping route. Adopt no new unobserved entrant into this patch, no entry by distant observed traffic, and no curb departure into this patch by the observed sidewalk pedestrians, including people at the left side-street corners and beside the right parked sedan. Sidewalk behavior, distant traffic and the rear intersection are otherwise outside this prototype, not certified safe or empty. This premise supports the local task and these entrant exclusions only. Actor BODY geometry and predictions, including portions outside this patch, are instead supported by the separately declared spatially unrestricted actor premises; no actor source or scenario cites this finite premise.

Adopt approximately level local pavement and the declared passenger-vehicle dimension priors. Estimate the road from the visible right curb, left curb and side-street opening, with their perspective continuation across the nearby pavement. Side-camera views support pavement beside the current footprint. The road rectangle is a finite longitudinal crop of approximately parallel curb-bounded roadway, including opposing and parking pavement, not an enlarged lane strip. Its 0.5 m uncertainty represents noncalibrated boundary and perspective error. The longitudinal crop edges are not physical curbs. Calibration establishes ray directions and ego axes, not certified monocular depth.

The reference image shows the black compact car turning across the forward roadway; preceding front images support the crossing interpretation. Adopt its reference center [12,1.3], 4.4 by 1.8 m body and yaw -0.65 rad. Over the next two seconds assume speed in [0,3] m/s, heading in [-0.9,0] rad, no reversal, and additionally center X in [12,18] and center Y in [-1.7,1.3] throughout. These are joint conditional bounds, not speed-only deductions. The adopted mode continues the turn; the adverse mode brakes while still obstructing the road. The common whole-interval rectangle encloses the complete rotating body for both modes, including all four reference corners. This premise applies to the actor's entire stated source geometry, including portions beyond the local road crop.

The silver sedan left of the black car faces the ego. Adopt its reference center [14.5,3.8] and 4.6 by 1.85 m body at yaw pi. Assume approach speed in [0,3] m/s, yaw within 0.15 rad of pi, center X in [8.5,14.5] and center Y in [3.3,4.3] throughout [0,2]. The adopted mode approaches slowly or pauses; the adverse mode approaches faster with lateral variation. The common source encloses the full body throughout both modes, including the reference pose. This premise applies without clipping at the road crop.

The right silver sedan and left silver wagon are positioned against their respective curbs. Conditionally assume both remain parked for two seconds, with no departure or door opening. Retain adverse pose variation up to 0.1 m per center axis and 0.03 rad yaw relative to their native poses. Each source encloses the corresponding complete body-pose family, including its nominal reference corners. Dimension priors are 4.8 by 1.85 m for the right sedan and 4.7 by 1.8 m for the left wagon. This premise supports the complete sources even where they extend beyond the finite road crop.

The front-left image shows the silver SUV at the side-street mouth 0.0076049 s before reference. Estimate its capture-time body center as [5.0,8.8] in fixed reference axes using image bearing, body-size prior, supplied camera orientation and capture ego pose. For this short past interval adopt a conditional speed bound of 1 m/s for both retained future scenarios, consistent with its waiting/creeping approach appearance. Evidence-to-reference displacement is then at most 0.008 m. The equal nominal reference center is an alignment estimate, not a measurement of stationarity. The 0.2 m alignment residual includes image-location and alignment error. This past premise is separate from future motion coverage.

Adopt a reference center [5.0,8.8], 4.6 by 1.9 m SUV and yaw -pi/2. Conditionally assume it waits or creeps toward the main road at speed no greater than 1 m/s. Jointly bound yaw within 0.1 rad of -pi/2, center X in [4.9,5.1] and center Y in [6.8,8.8]. The adverse mode creeps the full two meters. The common source encloses the entire oriented body over both modes, including all reference corners, not merely the center path. This premise supports the whole source, including its side-street portion outside the modeled road polygon.

anchors.rationale: The individually visible black compact hatchback/crossover supplies an oblique side-body extent. The adopted 4.4 m length matches its native body hypothesis and is a conditional class-size prior, not a measured specification.
The individually visible frontal silver sedan supplies a second perspective anchor using an adopted typical sedan width matching its native body hypothesis.
The nearby curbside sedan's visible oblique body supports the adopted midsize-sedan length and a perspective consistency check on the right curb distance.

metric_scale_support.metric_reasoning: In the 1600-pixel reference front image, the black car spans roughly 370 pixels obliquely across the lower central roadway. Its adopted 4.4 m length, oblique orientation and focal length near 1253 pixels support a rough low-teens-meter range, modeled as X=12 m. The frontal oncoming sedan's roughly 160-pixel width gives a comparable range around 14–15 m under the 1.85 m width prior. Bearings relative to the principal point place both left of ego, with the oncoming sedan farther left. The closer right parked sedan and visible curb support the approximate right boundary Y=-6.2 m; the left curb and side opening support Y=7 m over the finite road crop. Side-camera pavement observations support continuation beside the current footprint. These estimates combine perspective and conditional body dimensions; calibration alone does not certify their scale. Road and actor residuals remain nonzero and uncalibrated.

capture.navigation_intent: Continue along the visible drivable road when permissible; obey visible signals and yield as needed. No map or future ego route is supplied.

acquisition_metadata.vehicle_parameters_source: EXPERIMENT_ASSUMPTIONS, not measured nuScenes vehicle geometry; the same center offset is used in runtime calibration and offline evaluation
